series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #22 (the 2 PM slot)
hook: Your afternoon crash starts at lunch, and it's eating your goal.

gate.goal_link: goal work (study, side project) planned for after lunch fails in the dip; people read it as laziness and quit
gate.mechanism: post-lunch dip: circadian alertness dip in the early afternoon (occurs even without a meal), deepened by large meals and inactivity; a 10-min brisk walk raised self-rated energy for up to ~2 h (Thayer 1987, said as 'in one study')

frame.want: study / work on a goal every day
frame.obstacle: the session sits in the afternoon dip
frame.fix: hardest goal task before lunch, 10-min walk after lunch, easy work (emails) at 2:30

hooks_considered.line: Your afternoon crash starts at lunch, and it's eating your goal.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y, muted Y (alertness bars, red 2:30 'goal' bar), sendable Y, payoff Y; keeps ill-mixed-practice's promise

hooks_considered.line: If your goal is planned for 2 PM, you picked your worst hour.
You're not lazy at 2:30. You're scheduled wrong.

beats.hard_truth: 0.0 s alertness bars, 2:30 bar red 'Goal', chip 'Your goal is planned here'
